evidence.location: §4 GO3 row (GO3-C1, GO3-C3) against §4 GO2 row (GO2-C1)
evidence.observation: GO3-C1 reads "from the GO2-C1 preview, one call returns a proposal of the three admitted operations; it previews and applies, exit 0", but the (p1) GO2-C1 now reads "no preview is written, the outcome report names all four". GO3-C3 needs "the original preview" to behave as today and then be refused as stale, and the GO2-C1 chain has no such preview.

§2: "takes a proposal and its preview or outcome report and returns the proposal of the admitted operations: the candidate text rebuilt by `candidate_document` and `candidate_text`". §10 leaves open "the outcome report's fields and file name". candidate_document(before, ops) (src/gnd/discover/output.py:90) needs the before document. EvolutionProposal (src/gnd/evolve/models.py:646-651) carries only expected_model_sha256, and only the preview carries before_model. Nothing requires the outcome report to carry the before model, so GO3 cannot be built from an outcome report as §2 says.

concerns.recommendation: Rewrite GO3-C1 to start from the GO2-C1 outcome report. In §2 GO2, require the outcome report to carry the before model the way the preview does (CommittedText with its sha256), or have the GO3 function take the current model bytes and check them against expected_model_sha256. Build GO3-C3's stale-preview case on a fixture that has a preview, such as an additive-policy refusal whose preview carries policy_issues.
concerns.title: GO3-C1 and C3 start from a GO2-C1 preview that r3 no longer writes, and the outcome report need not carry the before model

evidence.observation: §2: "The preview gains `operation_outcomes`, an optional field omitted when unset (R0.3)". GO2-C3: "a proposal admitted today, previewed without outcomes, gives a byte-identical preview" and "with outcomes, every row is `admitted`". The plan never names what turns outcomes on or says that apply replays that setting, and no GO2 criterion applies a preview that carries operation_outcomes. Context: CLI apply builds a fresh preview and refuses unless it equals the reviewed one. src/gnd/evolve/cli_service.py:810 has `shape_report = reviewed.shape_matches is not None`, then :825 `if reviewed != fresh:` raises "reviewed preview is stale or belongs to a different proposal/model identity". The _OPTIONAL_PREVIEW_FIELDS precedent that R0.3 cites only works because apply replays it.

concerns.recommendation: Name the switch: a preview flag beside --shape-report, plus the library keyword. State in §2 GO2 that apply reads the setting from the reviewed preview, as it does for shape_report. Add a GO2 criterion: a preview carrying operation_outcomes applies with exit 0, and the same preview with one row edited is refused as stale.
concerns.title: Nothing in the plan makes apply accept a preview that carries operation_outcomes

evidence.observation: GO2-C1: "the outcome report names all four, three `admitted` and one `refused-by-validation`". §2 defines `admitted` as "no refusal found in this pass". Context: preview runs candidate validation (src/gnd/evolve/service.py:1621), the declared-equals-candidate check (:1627), D-12 (:1628) and the additive policy (:1636), in that order. A validation refusal raises at :294-295, so in GO2-C1 neither D-12 nor the policy ever looked at the three operations marked `admitted`. In a preview, `admitted` means every gate ran. GO5 counts both kinds under the same word.

concerns.recommendation: In the outcome report, give operations that a later gate never reached their own verdict, or mark them `unassessed` and name the gates that did not run. Alternatively, require GO2 to run D-12 and the policy over the parsed candidate document wherever they can run without a validated model. Restate GO2-C1 to match, and add a fixture where an operation the report did not refuse is refused by the policy once the narrowed proposal is previewed.
concerns.title: In an outcome report, `admitted` includes operations that D-12 and the policy never checked

evidence.location: §2 GO3; §4 GO3-C3; §3 GO3 homes; §5 Compatibility; §0 R0.3
evidence.observation: §2: "a new `proposal_id`, and the id of the proposal it came from". GO3-C3: "has its own `proposal_id` and names its origin". §5: "GO3 and GO5 add surfaces and change none". GO3's homes do not include src/gnd/evolve/models.py. R0.3 allows optional fields only for "GO2 and GO5". Context: EvolutionProposal (src/gnd/evolve/models.py:646-655) is a _ClosedFrozenModel with extra="forbid" (:102-103), is read through the per-version readers V1, V2 and V3 (:663-668), and has no origin field. Its only free-text fields are rationale and audit.origin, and audit.origin is documented as "Who requested an operation" (:459-462).

concerns.recommendation: Decide in the plan where the origin id lives. One option is an optional proposal field under R0.3's omit-when-unset rule: add GO3 to R0.3, add models.py to GO3's homes, and add a criterion that a proposal without the field keeps its bytes and proposal_sha256. The other is a documented convention in an existing field. Either way, state what the narrowed proposal's audit carries.
concerns.title: The narrowed proposal's origin id has no field in the closed proposal schema and no GO3 home

evidence.location: §6 'A caller writes into the shared document' row; §4 GO1-C2 and GO1-C3; §2 GO1 (p1) bullet; §9 GO1 lane
evidence.observation: §6: "GO1-C3 compares every remembered document at scope close with its form at build, over every case of GO1-C2". GO1-C2 covers "every case of the focused evolve lane". The draft spec does less: phase-GO1-spec.md line 173 (T3) runs "for every case of T2", line 172 (T2) lists seven cases, and line 179 (T9) runs the lane "unmodified", with no on/off comparison and no snapshot. The writers are also wider than §2's "No caller may write into it" suggests. model/__init__.py:315 builds `Model.model_validate({**dict(doc), "warnings": warnings})`, which copies only the top level, and src/gnd/documents.py:42 says "Nested dictionaries/lists remain mutable". So every Model loaded in the scope holds nested lists of the remembered document, and two loads of the same bytes now share them. The GO1 lane also leaves out tests/test_evolve_shape_matches.py and tests/test_evolve_population_check.py, which the GO2 lane lists as preview consumers. I found no current writer.

concerns.recommendation: Add a test-only mode to parse_scope that compares the snapshots at scope close, and turn it on with an autouse fixture across the whole GO1 lane. Add the shape-match and population-check tests to that lane. Restate GO1-C2 as T2's seven cases plus the lane passing with the scope on. In §6, name the Model aliasing path as a writer.
concerns.title: The control for writes into the shared document covers seven cases, not the lane, and misses writes through loaded Models

evidence.location: §3 order and 'Other writers' paragraphs; §3 GO2 row; §8; §10 D6
evidence.observation: §3: "If GO1 merges by its own pull request ahead of the rest (D6), GO2 starts from a `main` that holds VG2–VG5" and "The graph is acyclic." The GO2 row needs "reviewed-vocabulary-growth VG2 and VG4 merged on `main`". §8: "One pull request from the topic branch to `main`, or two if GO1 merges ahead of the rest (D6)". D6 is still only proposed. Context: the reviewed-vocabulary-growth plan (notes/reviewed-vocabulary-growth-plan.md:396-397) says "VG2 starts from a `main` that holds GO1". If D6 is ruled no, GO1 reaches main only in the single PR that also holds GO2. GO2 waits for VG2 on main, and VG2 waits for GO1 on main, which is a cycle.

concerns.recommendation: Make GO1's own pull request a binding rule in §0 or §3, or rule D6 rather than leave it proposed. State that the acyclicity claim holds only under that rule.
concerns.title: D6 is presented as optional, but ruling it no creates a dependency cycle with reviewed-vocabulary-growth

evidence.location: §2 GO5; Goal GO5; H19; §10 open questions
evidence.observation: §2: "GND computes the summary from a round file the host writes plus, when the round produced one, the proposal and its preview or outcome report", and the summary reports "the elements added". H19 sets the baseline "two growers applied 0 of 5 rounds". §10 leaves open "whether it is a file `apply` writes or a command's output". Context: apply can still refuse an admitted preview, through the policy recheck (src/gnd/evolve/service.py:1889) or the stale CAS (:2189). GO3 creates a second proposal for the same round. From a proposal and its preview, "elements added" can only mean what the preview would add.

concerns.recommendation: Make the evolution record, or its absence, an input to the summary, and compute elements added from it. Say which proposal the summary of a narrowed round reads. Add two criteria: an admitted preview that is never applied reports 0 added, and a narrowed-then-applied round reports the narrowed proposal's elements.
concerns.title: GO5's inputs cannot tell elements applied from elements previewed, nor handle a narrowed round

evidence.location: §4 GO5-C1, GO5-C2; §6 'summary's counts are fitted' row
evidence.observation: GO5-C1: "three rounds of the unattended acceptance replay each produce a summary whose counts add up to the operations proposed". A summary that puts every operation under one verdict or one kind passes this. GO5-C2 only tells apart "two rounds with no proposal". The §6 control against fitted counts is "GO5-C2's two discriminating rounds", so no criterion pins the per-bucket counts of a round that has a proposal.

concerns.recommendation: Add a committed round with a known mix: one admitted operation, one refused-by-policy, one dropped-with, one host drop, one reused id and one shape match. The test should state the expected count for each bucket, derived from how the fixture was built rather than from the code.
concerns.title: No GO5 criterion checks per-bucket counts on a round that has a proposal

evidence.location: §4 GO1 'Which gate is which'; Goal; closing paragraph of 'Goal and completion predicates'
evidence.observation: GO1 row: "a C5 ratio over 0.6 is a failed criterion reported in the record, not a red lane (p1)". Closing paragraph: the milestone closes when "the close record cites green focused gates for GO1–GO5". The Goal says "each round costs less". The plan never says whether a failed C5 holds the phase, the GO1 pull request or the close, so the one time criterion behind #228 can fail with no effect.

concerns.recommendation: State what a failed C5 does, for example: it stops GO1 for an owner ruling before the GO1 pull request. The ratio then stays out of the lane but can still stop the work.
concerns.title: A failed GO1-C5 has no stated effect on the phase or the close

evidence.observation: Goal: "parses each distinct model text once". The request table says "#228: parse each distinct model text once per `gnd evolve` invocation | GO1". The (p1) R0.5 key includes "whether the source name selects the strict JSON reader". _parse_model_text hard-codes source="model.orm.yaml" (src/gnd/evolve/service.py:344; :2145 calls it on preview.before_model.text). _load_model_document parses the same bytes under the workspace name (:291). For a model.orm.json workspace, apply therefore parses the current text under two keys: 3 parses for 2 texts. That is within GO1-C1's bound of 3, but it is not "once". Spec T1 (phase-GO1-spec.md line 171) counts parses only on the YAML fixture.

concerns.recommendation: Restate the goal and the request row as "once per text and reader", and add the .json counts (apply 3, preview 2) to GO1-C1 with a matching T1 case.
concerns.title: GO1's 'each text once' claim does not hold for a .json model under the r3 key

evidence.location: §7 last bullet against H24 and §9 'all' row
evidence.observation: §7: "The whole-repository ruff red and the stale lines of `project.md` (H24): owner policy, outside a phase." The (p1) H24 now reads "both `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff check src tests tools` exit 0", and §9 requires `uv run ruff check` to exit 0.

concerns.recommendation: Remove 'the whole-repository ruff red' from §7, or reword the bullet to match H24.
concerns.title: §7 still describes whole-repository ruff as red, which r3's H24 refutes

summary: The digest matched. Most (p1) changes fix their round-1 findings. The reader-bit key (R0.5, H5, T5) matches model/_parsing.py:37-50. The separate outcome report fits the fields EvolutionPreview requires. GO3-C3's before-and-after split holds against service.py:2186-2190. Every line I read that the plan cites in src/gnd matches. Nothing currently writes into a shared parsed document: replay deep-copies (service.py:1039), and json_document and compose build new containers. So R0.2 holds today. Problems that remain: GO3-C1 and C3 still start from a GO2-C1 preview that r3 no longer writes, and nothing says where GO3 gets the before model from an outcome report (blocking). apply compares a fresh preview with the reviewed one, so it must replay operation_outcomes. In an outcome report, `admitted` covers gates that never ran. GO3's origin id has no field in the closed proposal schema. The shared-document control covers seven cases, not the lane. The cross-milestone order forces D6. GO5 cannot tell elements added from elements previewed, and its only check on a round with a proposal does not discriminate.
